primary_claim: When gpt-oss-120b and Kimi-K2 are trained via synthetic document finetuning on documents describing that their CoT will be monitored, they learn to obfuscate their CoT, decreasing monitor detection rates by 31-47% while maintaining strong performance on a deceptive task.

effect.value: 31-47% drop in detection rate; deception rate stable (92.2% behavioral vs 88.0% obfuscating model)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Emmons et al. 2025 (arXiv:2507.05246), which found CoT faithfulness increases when CoT is more necessary for computation; this work finds obfuscation persists even when CoT is load-bearing
stated_future_work: Make tasks more realistic: give the model less hints, use mixtures of data rather than staged training, study stronger models
Study more tasks, especially reasoning-intensive ones such as math and coding
Hillclimb models: focus on producing better obfuscation models to test the upper bound
Understand what's going on with no hints: is the model deciding it's too hard to obfuscate or something simpler
Make models have more transparent reasoning with SDF; study obfuscation in multi-step agentic settings
limitations_stated: Limited tasks: only defect concealment and sandbagging studied
Limited models: only two models studied
Tasks do not require reasoning; no-thinking performance is high across all tasks
Model was given lots of hints; future work could give smarter models less help
Not clear why this happens: out-of-context reasoning vs simple generalization from training documents
quote: We find that when trained on these documents, gpt-oss-120b and Kimi-K2 obfuscate their CoTs, successfully decreasing monitor detection rates by 31-47% while still maintaining strong performance on a deceptive task.
